+   queries or IDs refuse the suite with the colliding IDs, never silent merging.

+   first `floor(0.2n)` (at least 2) to test, the next `floor(0.2n)` (at least 2) to
+   validation, the rest to train (at least 2). Seed and membership by case ID are
+   recorded. Mode `holdout` therefore needs >=6 cases per label; smaller populations
+   are refused, never shrunk to an empty partition. Mode `test-selection` (upstream
+   parity, >=4 per label: first `floor(0.4n)` (at least 2) selection, rest train) must be named so in every output;
+   its selection score is never reported as generalization.

+   `triggered`/`not-triggered` repetitions count; a case passes when the trigger rate

+   inconclusive/technical repetition is `unresolved`: it counts as failed and is reported.

+   validation passes; ties by fewer unresolved, then higher train passes, then the
+   earliest candidate (original first). Original/best/last are reported separately.

+   zero unresolved; otherwise at the iteration limit (proposed 5). Bounds known before
+   execution: trigger runs <= (iterations + 1) * (|train| + |validation|) * r + 2 * |test| * r,
+   proposal calls <= iterations (plus at most one shortening each, ap-x8p7.5). Exceeding
+   a bound stops with an explicit reason.
+ - **Holdout:** test is evaluated exactly once, after selection, for original and best
+   only; it never enters the proposer payload, selection, stopping or history replay.
+   The proposer receives train cases/results only (no validation or test detail).
+ 
+ | Example | Per label (trigger / no-trigger) | Outcome |
+ |---|---|---|
+ | 5 / 8 cases, mode holdout | 5 < 6 | refused: population too small |
+ | 10 / 10 cases, mode holdout | test 2, validation 2, train 6 each | accepted |
+ | 4 / 4 cases, mode test-selection | selection 2, train 2 each | accepted, labelled test-selection |
+ | r=3, should-trigger: triggered, triggered, technical | case unresolved | failed, blocks early stop |
+ | validation 7/8 vs 7/8, unresolved 0 vs 1 | tie broken | candidate with 0 unresolved wins |
+ 
+ Not claimed: generalization beyond the frozen population, model-independence, or
+ any automatic application of the best description to the Skill source.
+

+ 
+ Pre-registration (provisional thresholds, owner approval pending), method
+ `judge-calibration-v1`. Human blind labels are the reference; the Judge is measured.
+ 
+ - **Corpus:** explicit decisive grades from retained verified attempts, exported as a
+   workspace into a private directory outside the repository and outside the evaluation
+   data root (export refuses that protected root). First corpus: campaign e079faf1,
+   12 trials, 85 criterion items, sampled by judge verdict (8 trials with a predicted
+   fail, 4 without) — this selection bias is reported, not corrected.

+   labels, made without seeing `grading.json`, the sealed prediction key or a report.
+ - **Metrics:** confusion of human label versus Judge verdict; coverage (labelled/total);
+   decisive agreement; false-pass rate (Judge pass among human fail — the costly error);
+   false-fail rate (Judge fail among human pass); human-undecidable count. Unlabelled
+   items are missing coverage, never agreement; empty denominators are unavailable.
+ - **Proposed thresholds:** coverage >= 0.90, decisive agreement >= 0.90, false-pass
+   <= 0.10, false-fail <= 0.10. They describe one judge configuration on one campaign;
+   no efficacy, model-quality or generalization claim follows.

+   grades without candidate relaunch; it needs explicit paid-run permission.

content.text: Skills are reusable sets of instructions and resources that teach goose how to perform specific tasks. A skill can range from a simple checklist to a detailed workflow with domain expertise, and can include supporting files like scripts or templates. Example use cases include deployment procedures, code review checklists, and API integration guides. :::info This functionality uses the built-in Skills platform extension, which is enabled by default. ::: When a session starts, goose adds discovered skill names and descriptions to its instructions. During the session, goose can load a skill's full instructions when: - Your request clearly matches a skill's purpose - You explicitly ask to use a skill, for example: - "Use the code-review skill to review this PR" - "Follow the new-service skill to set up the auth service" - "Apply the deployment skill" You can also ask goose what skills are available, run `goose skills list`, or use the CLI `/skills` command to list available skills and load one or more by name: ```bash /skills code-review edge-case-finder ``` :::info Claude Compatibility goose skills are compatible with Claude Desktop and other [agents that support Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/home#adoption). ::: ## Built-in Skills goose ships with a built-in skill that is always available without any installation: | Skill | Description | |-------|-------------| | `web-search` | Search the web using DuckDuckGo (no API key), Tavily, or SearXNG, and extract page content. | 194: * Load an agent's instructions into the current conversation 213:* Hook Payload 896: * DictationDownloadProgress {#schema-dictationdownloadprogress} 900: * DictationModelDownloadProgressRequest_unstable {#schema-dictationmodeldownloadprogressrequest_unstable} 901: * DictationModelDownloadProgressResponse_unstable {#schema-dictationmodeldownloadprogressresponse_unstable} 902: * DictationModelDownloadRequest_unstable {#schema-dictationmodeldownloadrequest_unstable} 972: * LocalInferenceDownloadProgressDto {#schema-localinferencedownloadprogressdto} 973: * LocalInferenceDownloadState {#schema-localinferencedownloadstate} 982: * LocalInferenceModelDownloadCancelRequest_unstable {#schema-localinferencemodeldownloadcancelrequest_unstable} 983: * LocalInferenceModelDownloadProgressRequest_unstable {#schema-localinferencemodeldownloadprogressrequest_unstable}

# Current Goose hook contract

For ordinary requests use current stable Goose and current official documentation:
[Hooks](https://goose-docs.ai/docs/guides/context-engineering/hooks) and
[Plugins](https://goose-docs.ai/docs/guides/context-engineering/plugins).
Read on 2026-11-07. Exact host versions and historical evidence live in the separate
[compatibility matrix](compatibility-matrix.md); they are not alternate default workflows.

## Native layout and authoring

Use `<plugin>/hooks/hooks.json` and contained executable command handlers.
Distributor namespaces are not native activation paths. Multiple layouts are rejected;
review preserves native hooks and blocks adapter-only migration without verified
activation. New component authoring must preserve manifest bytes unless a manifest
change is separately authorized. Structural review never proves lifecycle activation.
No retired creator init/validator command supplies that proof.

## Events and failure policy

Only PreToolUse and Stop are blocking events. `PreToolUseResult` is observation only;
it cannot change allow/deny. Matching observers are awaited and can add latency;
best-effort delivery is not durable audit evidence. Matchers are regular expressions,
not globs; anchor exact matches. Never log secrets in payloads or denial reasons.

Current command actions accept `on_failure` for PreToolUse: `allow` is the default,
`block` explicitly denies when a matching hook fails without a recognized decision.
This field is ignored for other events; Stop failures remain fail-open.
Explicit denial uses exit 2 with stderr reason or a documented block decision on stdout.
Ordinary nonzero exits are not themselves denial. Keep stdout for the decision and
stderr for diagnostics. Check the current documented protocol before modifying handlers.

## Verification boundary

Source documentation, direct handler tests and observed host activation are distinct.
Record running host version and actual checks; unavailable runtime evidence remains
unverified. Refresh official documentation and implementation before changing a public
contract. Historical snapshots remain retained format evidence, not current tooling.

# Distribution status

The current installation is the Git-backed main tree, containing independently
installable Skills and the skill-creator Node.js >=22.22.2 launcher/runtime.
See [README](README.md) for installation and [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development.

The pre-migration Bun creator executables, native archives, tagged native workflow
and local staged installer have been retired and removed from current tooling.
No native compatibility or newly published release is claimed by this cleanup.
Historical compatibility evidence and third-party/vendor sources remain retained.

## Unreleased — native keyring verification (ap-44kd)

Version not yet assigned; classify at publication (backward-compatible fix: PATCH).

- **Fix — macOS keyring consent:** Goose-created Keychain items trust only Goose, so
  reading them through `/usr/bin/security` waits for a user consent dialog. The reader
  now allows 60 s on macOS (10 s elsewhere); choose "Always Allow" or export the provider
  variable for non-interactive runs. `security -w` hexadecimal output (non-ASCII
  secrets) is now decoded.
- **CI — native keyring verification:** `native-keyring.yml` writes a synthetic entry with
  keyring-rs 3.6.3 (the library Goose uses) on macOS and Windows runners and reads it
  through the shipped runtime. Windows verified; macOS consent behavior verified.

## 0.10.0 — activation oracle, comparison dashboard, sandbox and keyring credentials

Observed in a Goose 1.57.0 code-mode session on installed 0.8.3 (source 7d13c23):

## 0.8.4 — functional Goose Skill loading

PATCH release: instruction and documentation corrections only; no CLI, option,
default or runtime change.

- Routing Skills (plugin-creator, plugin-script-packaging, agent-creator,
  hook-creator) name the functional Goose call: `load_skill` with the installed
  name, through `execute_javascript` `tools.call("load_skill", { name })` when it is
  not a direct tool. Goose `load` and `delegate(source:)` resolve recipes,
  subrecipes and agents, never Skills; a direct `SKILL.md` read is disclosed as
  reading, not activation. Fixes an observed misroute to `load` on Goose 1.57.0.
- skill-creator authoring guidance adds functional cross-Skill routing.
- skill-creator evaluation design maps Skill intentions to independent scenario
  evidence (ap-fxyc).
- Static regression test only; natural-activation behavior is not measured. See the
  [versioned compatibility evidence](skills/plugin-creator/references/compatibility-matrix.md#084--functional-goose-skill-loading-2026-11-19).

  `crates/goose/src/agents/reply_parts.rs` keeps tools of first-class platform

  shows the same set. The observation contradicts the source reading; the cause is not
  established (a different build path is possible) and no upstream issue was filed.

routing as much as the Skill description. Activation results are only comparable

Les 7 jobs sont au vert, puis fusionnée. | | **#98** essais d'activation (ap-x8p7.13) | ✅ Fusionnée. J'ai d'abord dû intégrer `develop` deux fois et résoudre des conflits :
• `handle-export-command.ts` : j'ai gardé à la fois le refus des campagnes d'activation et l'injection de la télémétrie ;

Les hooks Entire appellent d'abord Entire, puis l'intégration beads (déplacée dans `*.pre-entire`). | | **ap-qbol** | ✅ Analysé, documenté et fermé (**PR #100**, fusionnée, voir le détail ci-dessous). | | **Feuille de calibration** | ⏳ Toujours 0 sur 85. Il faut que tu la labellises. | | ap-37dw | Déjà fermé. | ### ap-qbol : ce que j'ai trouvé - **Documentation Goose** (pages using-skills et code-mode) : elle ne précise pas si `load_skill` reste un outil directement appelable en mode code. - **Code source de Goose v1.57.0** : l'extension `skills` est déclarée prioritaire, et le mode code conserve en principe ces extensions comme outils directs. `load_skill` devrait donc rester accessible directement. - **Ce qu'on observe** : dans les logs de requête de la campagne 9c1cef33, `load_skill` ne fait pas partie des outils directs, et c'est pareil dans cette session. Ça contredit le code source. Je n'ai pas trouvé la cause. - **Conséquence** : en mode code, les essais où la Skill devrait se déclencher mesurent surtout la façon dont Goose route les outils. Ces résultats ne sont comparables qu'entre campagnes ayant le même réglage du mode code. - **Où c'est documenté** : dans la matrice de compatibilité de plugin-creator et dans la section « Unreleased » de `RELEASES.md`. ### ⚠️ Deux points à connaître 1. **Commits bloqués par Entire.** Avec `-m`, le hook `prepare-commit-msg` d'Entire attend une réponse dans le terminal, et mes commits sont restés bloqués plusieurs minutes. Ça marche en lançant git avec `setsid -w`, sans désactiver les hooks. J'ai noté l'astuce dans `bd remember`. 2. **Push automatique des logs de session.** Le hook `pre-push` d'Entire envoie `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` vers `upstream`, qui est ton dépôt personnel. Un checkpoint y est déjà. Vérifie que c'est voulu, car ces logs peuvent contenir le contenu des sessions. Le remote peut se changer dans `.entire/settings.local.json`. ### Ce qui reste - **Nouveaux tickets prêts :** - **ap-49tf** : enregistrer dans les métadonnées des campagnes si le mode code est actif. Une décision t'attend : on se contente de l'enregistrer, ou on ajoute une option pour fixer ce réglage ? - **ap-y2f2** : signaler le problème à l'équipe Goose (aaif-goose). feat(oi-kit): add SkillOperation and drop the Skills extension
2026-11-17T03:43:51Z
Closes #13481.

Builds on #13566 (tool hooks fired from the run loop) and #13571 (chat mode removed), both on main.

## What changed

- **oi-kit** gets `SkillOperation` and a `SkillSource` trait (`crates/goose-agent/src/skills/operation.rs`). The operation lists the host's skills in the system prompt, advertises `load_skill`, answers `load_skill` calls that approval marked executable (arguments and supporting files included), and offers `/skills` and `/<skill-name> args`. The host supplies the skills and reads supporting files. Hooks come from the host's run loop, so the operation has no hook code.
- **goose** implements `SkillSource` with `GooseSkillSource`: discovery, the `{{GOOSE_DOCS_ROOT}}` substitution, and the confined supporting-file reader with the symlink fix from #13531. It supplies the help text `/skills` shows when nothing is installed.
- `SkillsClient`, the Skills platform extension and the `tools_excluding(skills)` special cases in tool calling are removed. Stale `skills` entries in config are already skipped by `is_extension_available`.
- `SlashCommandOperation` gets the operations with skills last, so built-in commands and recipes win name clashes (covered by `builtin_commands_win_over_skills_and_recipes`).
- Code Mode keeps `load_skill` as a direct tool.

## Behaviour changes

- Skills can no longer be turned off through the Skills extension.
- `load_skill` reads skills from the session's working directory. It no longer uses the extension lease, so the two lease tests for skills are removed.
- The `unadvertised_load_skill_is_not_confirmed_or_loaded` test is replaced by `load_skill_stays_a_direct_tool_in_code_mode`.
- `load_skill` calls no longer get a goose `execute_tool` tracing span.

## Verification

- New oi-kit integration test `crates/goose-agent/tests/skill_operation.rs`: approved calls with arguments, a supporting file and an unknown skill are answered, and an unapproved call is left alone; `/review` renders the skill with arguments through `SlashCommandOperation`.
- `GooseSkillSource` tests read a nested supporting file and one under a symlinked directory.
- `cargo test -p goose --lib --features code-mode -- state_machine skills slash_command platform_extensions`: 361 passed, including the new `load_skill_stays_a_direct_tool_in_code_mode` and `builtin_commands_win_over_skills_and_recipes`.
- `cargo test -p goose-agent`: all pass.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings`: clean apart from the macOS-only `request_log_permissions_test` error that is also on main.

content.text:
## Activation trials — ap-x8p7.13

`agent-plugin activation` (`handle-activation-command.ts`) runs query-only "with"
trials: `use-cases/run-activation-trials.ts` `prepareActivationTrials()` (profile
loaded with `suites: false`, queries via `filesystem/activation-case-source.ts`) →
`executeEvaluation(..., "activation")` → `observeActivationCampaign()` (verified
reader + `GooseActivationObserver` on the case's target Skill only) →
`reporting/activation-result-writer.ts`. Pure rules live in `domain/activation-trial.ts`.
Plans are schema 5 (`mode`, `cases`, `queriesSha256`); `shouldTrigger` never enters
scenarios, options or `TrialRequest`. Grading/export refuse activation campaigns.
Outputs carry case IDs, never query text. See product §37.
## Multi-campaign dashboard — ap-r5dg

`generate-dashboard.mjs` imports `verifiedExport()`/`buildReportData()` from
`generate-report.mjs` and requires at least two distinct explicit export roots
(`--workspace` repeated) plus a mandatory new `--output` (no owning campaign, no
default). It writes exclusively (`wx`, 0600) outside every export/protected root
into `../assets/dashboard-viewer.html`. `campaignColumn()` keys cells by
[source, scenarioId, host]; `compareCells()` emits a With-profile delta only for
the same profile id+revision, one equal prompt/criteria fingerprint, one equal
judge configuration, one equal candidate host, and known different configured
models with non-null scores. Same-model campaigns are shown side by side as
replications, never pooled. Technical/inconclusive cells stay null, never zero.
Judge/host provenance lacking a version is unknown and blocks deltas; a judge with
configured-default (effective unknown) model qualifies a delta with a caveat.
Unequal selected/planned With coverage also qualifies a delta (ap-t7uo), never refuses it.
`boundReview()` links a sibling `review.html` only if it embeds this export's
manifest digest and any `.agent-plugin-html.json` receipt matches campaign/bytes.
Evidence links target a sibling `review.html#trial=<id>` only when it exists;
the report viewer opens that exact selected trial or keeps the overview. No
model, database or network calls; activation counts are displayed, not compared.
| Activation option | Contract |
|---|---|
| `--skills` / `--plugin <paths...>` | Same profile semantics as evaluation |
| `--queries <file>` | Required unless `--resume`: `{"cases":[{"id","query","should_trigger","skill"?}]}` or bare `[{"query","should_trigger"}]` (ids `1`,`2`,…); 4 MiB, ≤1000 cases; `skill` (profile Skill directory) required with several Skills; duplicate ids or normalized queries refuse the file |
| `--agent goose` | Only Goose has an activation oracle |
| `--model`, `--repetitions`, `--parallelism`, `--max-turns`, `--timeout` | As evaluation; defaults 3, 3, 10, 300 |
| `--sandbox <none\|bubblewrap>` | Default `bubblewrap`; `none` keeps private HOME/XDG only |
| `--registry`, `--output` | As evaluation (Hive campaign layout) |

Les deux tâches sont traitées. Pour ap-49tf, la PR #101 est prête, avec la CI au vert sur les 7 jobs, mais je ne l'ai pas fusionnée.

## ap-y2f2 : pas de ticket ouvert chez Goose, le problème est déjà corrigé
- **Cause dans Goose 1.57.0 :** le code exclut l'extension `skills` des outils proposés au modèle. Il réinjecte ensuite un `load_skill` sans extension propriétaire, que le mode code supprime aussitôt.
- **Correction :** la PR [aaif-goose/goose#13574](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/pull/13574), fusionnée le 17/11 et publiée dans **v1.60.0**, garde `load_skill` comme outil direct en mode code, avec un test dédié. J'ai vérifié que le code des versions 1.60.0 et 1.60.2 contient bien ce correctif.
- Signaler le problème aurait fait doublon. J'ai fermé le ticket et noté la cause et la version corrigée dans la matrice de compatibilité.
- Le binaire 1.60.x n'est pas testé ici, car tu as toujours la 1.57.0. J'ai créé un ticket de suivi pour le vérifier. Ça demande ton accord pour mettre Goose à jour et pour lancer une campagne payante.

## ap-49tf : enregistrer l'état du mode code dans les campagnes (PR #101, commit `ded9efd`)
J'ai tranché la question ouverte ainsi : **on enregistre le réglage et on refuse les essais si la config a changé, sans ajouter d'option en ligne de commande**. Pour choisir le réglage, on continue de modifier la config Goose.
- **Enregistrement :** chaque nouvelle campagne lit une fois si le mode code est actif dans la config Goose réellement transmise aux essais, et fige cette valeur dans le plan. Une reprise ne la relit jamais. Les campagnes plus anciennes restent marquées « inconnu », jamais « désactivé ».
- **Refus :** si la config Goose a changé depuis le début de la campagne, l'essai échoue avant le lancement, avec un message explicite.
- **Où on le voit :**
  - dans le résultat d'activation (`activation-run-v1`), avec une limitation quand le mode est actif ou inconnu ;
  - dans le rapport HTML (« Code mode »), qui refuse un export où la valeur ne correspond pas aux essais ;
  - dans le dashboard, qui refuse de calculer un écart entre deux campagnes aux réglages différents et ajoute une réserve si l'un des deux est inconnu ;
  - le benchmark refusait déjà de mélanger des campagnes aux options différentes.
- **Documentation mise à jour :** spécification produit (nouvelle section 38), cartes AGENTS, contrat de commande, matrice de compatibilité, et une entrée dans RELEASES classée MINOR (nouvelle fonctionnalité).

**Vérifications locales :**
- app : 432 tests (431 réussis, 1 ignoré), typecheck et lint OK ;
- runtime régénéré, contrôle de dérive et inventaire OK ;
- rapport : 15 tests réussis, 7 ignorés faute de navigateur ;
- dashboard : 7 réussis, 1 ignoré ;
- test:distribution : 21/21 ;
- groupes CI `quick` et `remaining` OK. `remaining` a d'abord échoué parce que le binaire Goose n'était pas indiqué ; il passe en ajoutant `GOOSE_EXECUTABLE`.

Je n'ai lancé aucune campagne payante.

- **Fusionner la PR #101 dans `develop` ?** Je ne l'ai pas fait sans ton accord. Le ticket ap-49tf reste ouvert jusque-là.
- Rien n'est publié sur `main`. Le travail est dans le worktree `../agent-plugins-49tf`.
